title: upscayl/upscayl
abstract:
v2.15 is out! 🥳 Download Now ⬇️ Special thanks to our sponsors: Warp, the intelligent terminal for developers Use images as AI context in your terminal! Requestly - Free & Open-Source alternative to Postman All-in-one platform to Test, Mock and Intercept APIs. 🆙 Upscayl Free and Open Source AI Image Upscaler Upscayl lets you enlarge and enhance low-resolution images using advanced AI algorithms.
Enlarge images without losing quality. It's almost like magic! 🎩🪄 https://upscayl.org Demo.Showcase.mp4 Contents 👨‍💻 Installation 🐧 Linux 🍎 macOS 🐌 Windows 👨‍🏫 Documentation - Tutorials and Guides ⚖️ Demo Results (Before and After) 🤫 Roadmap 🛠 Developing Upscayl 🤓 FAQ 🎁 Donate and support the project ❤ Credits 👨‍💻 Installation Important You'll need a Vulkan compatible GPU (Graphics Card) to upscale images. Many iGPUs (integrated graphics) do not work but, no harm in trying :) 🐧 Linux Upscayl should be available on the software listings of most Linux operating systems. Your distro's Store app might also support the Flatpak or Snap version. 💼 Portable Method Go to releases section or our official website . Download the upscayl-x.x.x-linux.AppImage file. Right Click AppImage -> Go to Permissions tab -> Check 'allow file to execute' and then double click the file to run Upscayl. You can also choose to install using other formats like RPM (Fedora), DEB (Debian/Ubuntu based), and ZIP (Any x86 Linux OS). 🍎 macOS (MacOS 12 and later) Link Go to releases section or our official website . Download the upscayl-x.x.x-mac.dmg file. Double click dmg, drag Upscayl icon into Applications folder. Open Finder, click 'Applications' tab in the left sidebar. Find Upscayl and right click on it. Select 'Open'. In the window that appears, press 'Open' yet again. 🍺 Homebrew brew install --cask upscayl 🐌 Windows (Windows 10 and later) Go to releases section or our official website . Download the upscayl-x.x.x-win.exe file. Double click exe file to launch. If you get a SmartScreen warning - click 'More Info' and then 'Run Anyway' OR press 'YES' on the unverified publisher dialog. Follow the installation steps. Profit! 👨‍🏫 Documentation - Tutorials and Guides Check out our Documentation here . Try out even more new models! Convert your own models Compatibility List Troubleshooting ⚖️ Results Check out Upscayl before/after comparisons here . 🤫 Roadmap You can track all the progress here: https://github.com/orgs/upscayl/projects/1 Fix bugs Make the whole world use FOSS (WIP 🚧) 🛠 Development I recommend using Volta: https://volta.sh for installing Node.js.
Download and install volta, then do: volta install node . 🏃 Running Note If you are not willing to install git , you can skip the first line, download the source zip and extract it to upscayl instead and carry on with the rest of the instructions. git clone https://github.com/upscayl/upscayl cd upscayl # INSTALL DEPENDENCIES npm install # RUN THE DEVELOPMENT SERVER LOCALLY # # YOUR LOGS WILL NOW APPEAR IN THE TERMINAL npm run start 🏗️ Building # INSTALL DEPENDENCIES npm install # PACKAGE THE APP npm run dist # PUBLISH THE APP, MAKE SURE TO ADD GH_TOKEN= IN SHELL # ONLY DO THIS IF YOU'RE A MAINTAINER npm run publish-app 🤓 FAQ How does Upscayl work? Upscayl uses AI models to enhance your images by guessing what the details could be. It uses Real-ESRGAN and Vulkan architecture to achieve this. Our backend is fully open-source under the AGPLv3 license. I don't see a drastic change in my upscaled image. Why is that? Upscayl can enhance low resolution images and images that are pixelated but it cannot de-blur or do focus adjustment on your image. If your image is out-of-focus or totally blurred, Upscayl is not the right tool for it. Please use images that are similar to the examples we've given here. Is there a CLI available? The CLI tool is called upscayl-ncnn . Do I need a GPU for this to work? Yes, unfortunately. NCNN Vulkan requires a Vulkan-compatible GPU. Upscayl won't work with most iGPUs or CPUs. But hey, no harm in trying ;) @Wyrdgirn has contributed a workaround for Windows and Linux in #390 ! Nobody knows how to manipulate the macOS and Haiku frameworks... I stopped the magic Batch Upscayl and my images haven't been processed, compressed, or are in the wrong scale! When a model doesn't support an action, Upscayl will finish upscayling all the images first before post-processing them. What this means is that you should simply wait for the process to finish. How can I contribute? You can report issues, fix code and add features by submitting PRs, or donate! 😊 What's the GPU ID for? It is for selecting which GPU to use. The specific procedure is detailed in the Wiki . Note that for Windows systems, if Upscayl is not set to performance mode, the system may override this setting. Where do I find more models? More models can be taken from here: https://github.com/upscayl/custom-models 🎁 Donate ❤ Credits Real-ESRGAN for their wonderful research work. Real-ESRGAN: Copyright (c) 2021, Xintao Wang @JanDeDinoMan, @xanderfrangos, @Fdawgs, @keturn for their code contributions @aaronliu0130 for providing community support :) Helaman for their HFA2k model (included as "High Fidelity") Foolhardy for their Remacri model . Kim2091 for their Ultrasharp and Ultramix Balanced model . @NicKoehler for their amazing logo :) Copyright © 2023 - Upscayl By Nayam Amarshe and TGS963 Made with 🖱 & ⌨

title: macro-inc/macro
abstract: Sign up · Docs · Book demo · Website · Feature requests · Contribute · Hiring Macro is the all-in-one workspace for you and your team. It unifies email + messages + docs + tasks + agents + CRM into a single fast interface with shared team-level memory. Everything in your workspace is @linked and searchable so your team (and your agents) never have to switch tools. Why Macro We built Macro because we wanted a single operating system for our startup. There are many good software products, and we used them all — Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, and Superhuman — but they don't work together as one system. As we scaled our last venture to ~20 people things started to break: every team got their own tools and the company was held together by MCP and Zapier. The company was not computable. It was chaotic. Macro is a complete redesign of work software from the ground up as a single system. Designed by us in NYC and Toronto, dogfooded by our team of ~15 for two years. Built in SolidJS and Rust for speed and reliability. We're focused on building something that any small company or team at a larger company can use as their "operating system". Features Macro is composed of 'blocks' designed to be modular, extensible, and work together like Lego. For each block, we studied the best prior art and tried to make it even better. Each surface is purpose-built for its job rather than composed from a generic block primitive — but every one of them shares the same backend; cross-references between a doc and a task, or a channel message and an email, are natively stored as a bidirectional graph . Block Docs What it does Email Docs → Multi-account unified inbox, keyboard shortcuts, and shared inboxes. Gmail. Messages Docs → Channels and direct messages designed for focused technical discussions. Tasks Docs → Linear-inspired tasks, tightly integrated with channels, email, and agents. Docs Docs → Real-time collaborative, markdown-native docs built on CRDTs, with @mentions. Canvas Docs → 2D board with embedded @links to tasks, files, and emails. Agents Docs → Unified, team-level memory. Can take action on your behalf. Calls Docs → Recorded, transcribed, and logged to team memory for agents. File storage Docs → Auto-imported from email and channels, fully searchable. Pull requests Docs → Linked to tasks, embeddable in channels, available to agents. CRM Docs → Customer and contact objects, custom properties, email sync, enrichment. Multiple email inboxes w/ good AI tools, integrated CRM Macro Mail is inspired by Superhuman's keyboard-first interface with a few key additions: Multi-account. Triage all your Google accounts in a single inbox, with the same tagging and sharing system. Or triage individually. Unified inbox: emails, messages, @mentions, and tasks to complete, all in the same list. Use j k and e to navigate everything. Better AI, with a tools/MCP surface designed to work across inboxes and to help your agents more accurately retrieve information. For example, we expose a unified search tool that allows agents to search all file attachment PDFs (parsed out of email) directly, rather than pulling email threads then attachments. You can also draft, edit and send emails right from AI chats, without opening your email. Multitasking ability — Macro has a built-in window manager that lets you create 3+ splits (scales with monitor size) so you can draft emails while reviewing prior threads. Company/Contact objects. Macro has native CRM capability so you can cmd+k to a contact, like tim@acme.com to see all emails between you and that person, or companies, to see all emails and files between everyone on your team and everyone at that company, e.g. @acme.com . All of this right from your email without having to open a heavyweight CRM like HubSpot or Salesforce. Email aggregation by contact or company is also available to your agents so they can better assist with CRM-type queries and actions. Macro Mail lives in the same interface as channels, docs, tasks, and code. From any email, hit "task" to create a linked task, e.g. a ticket for an engineer from a customer support email. @mention emails in documents, e.g. @Re: Contract Signature.eml inside of Todos.md. In Macro, your email is brought into the fold with all of your tools, and your team, in the same permissions system: just hit Share to share an email to any DM or channel — no need to screenshot. Email docs → Team chat for focused technical discussions Macro Chat is designed to be more focused than Slack. The first couple of replies show inline and the rest collapse into a thread, so a busy channel stays readable. Threads are permissioned severally so you can share threads across channels by copying links. Everything is stored in a bidirectional graph, so tasks @link to messages that created them, customer support emails tie into support channels, CRM records get updated when they're discussed in messages, etc. The core idea is that (i) messaging should be the centerpiece around which tasks, mail, docs, and content management are built, all in a lightweight way, and agents should be first-class citizens like human users and (ii) messaging needs to be more focused and readable for technical conversations, and not turn into battles where context is lost and progress is indistinguishable from noise. Messages docs → Task management built around chat Linear recently published a report that issue tracking is dead. We agree with that, but the stronger form is that issue tracking never really worked, at least for us. We really tried and we blamed ourselves, but as we talked to other companies, it turns out that nobody was using their issue tracker "correctly". And if that's the case, the problem is the design of the tool, not the companies that use it. The core problem with traditional issue trackers or project management tools is that they get out of date. The reason they get out of date is that (i) they're a separate system from where the conversation really happens in team chat (e.g. Slack, Macro, Discord, etc.) and (ii) they don't add much benefit beyond tracking the work. They're a chore with near-term costs and only the promise of long-term benefit. They're too rigid compared to a 2D canvas, too opinionated, and don't match how your project actually functions. The solution isn't to forgo tracking entirely. We tried that and it was a different form of chaos. The solution we've found is lightweight issues tightly coupled to your channels and DMs, so that issue tracking naturally occurs where the conversation itself happens. Creating tasks in Macro is easy. Where possible, tasks created are bidirectionally linked to the creating context (e.g. a customer email) so the full chain is auditable from "why are we doing this" → task → agent → pull request, all in one system. Create a task from an email From anywhere via c t From a markdown doc with /task From any - [ ] bullet by highlighting and clicking "Task" @Macro create tasks in any channel or DM In any agent chat Via external MCP, API or SDK Tasks docs → @linked markdown docs powered by CRDTs We wanted everything in a single markdown editor without switching tools. Native markdown compatibility and bulk/import export (see "file over app" paradigm) Live collaboration with CRDTs and Cloudflare durable objects make it feel like you're editing on the same computer. Edits come in ~instantly instead of ka-chunking like Google Docs Version control: history and forking, with a neat UI for scrubbing history. This is still in v1, there's a lot to do to get it closer to git, or we may eventually add git compatibility. Offline editing and reconciliation. @-linked to everything in your workspace: email, docs, tasks, messages, channels, companies, contacts, etc. Like Notion but multi-modal Mobile-friendly, in our iOS app or on the web (Android app coming soon) Agent native editing, powered by swarms of agents operating as peers in the CRDT collaboration system like human collaborators.

title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
abstract:
An AI that still works when the internet doesn't. Survival LLM is a free AI assistant and emergency library that runs entirely on your own computer. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn, or purify water, and it answers from trusted sources and shows you exactly where each answer came from. Download for Mac 212 MB Download for Windows 25 MB Source code Free and open source. Set it up while you have internet; after that it needs none. What it does Works with no internet The AI model and the library live on your computer. Nothing you ask leaves it. Shows its sources Every answer lists the articles it read. Click one to read it yourself, with the exact passage highlighted. Made for emergencies Medical references, FEMA and CDC guidance, survival manuals, how-to guides, repair guides and about 930,000 Wikipedia articles. Pick your version The app is the same everywhere. When it opens, it checks your computer's memory and downloads the AI model that fits. More memory means a smarter model. Your computer AI model it uses Our emergency test Model download Mac with 128 GB or more memory NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super 21 of 22 right 80 GB Mac with 32–96 GB Qwen3.8 27B 21 of 22 right 18 GB Windows PC with 32 GB or more NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 19 of 22 right 25 GB Mac or PC with 16–31 GB IBM Granite 4.2 8B 14 of 22 right 6 GB "Right" means it got the main point of official guidance right on 22 blackout and first-aid questions, graded blind, in our tests on an earlier build of the library ( how we tested ). Smaller models make more mistakes, so the app always shows the source to check. Plus the library: a 9 GB download for everything (19 GB once installed), or 1.3 GB (3 GB installed) without Wikipedia and iFixit. Free disk space needed: the model's size plus 5 GB, plus about 27 GB while the full library installs (10 GB for the smaller one). Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or newer) with macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, and 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. Set it up in three steps Setup takes 20 minutes to about 2½ hours, depending on your computer and your internet speed. You only click for about 5 minutes; the rest is downloading. Download Survival LLM for Mac or Windows and unzip it. On Windows, right-click the zip and choose Extract All . Open it. On a Mac, double-click Survival LLM . On Windows, open the extracted folder and double-click Survival LLM.bat . Follow the setup. The app opens in its own window and downloads the AI engine (built into the Mac app), the AI model that fits your computer, and the library. Let it finish while you're online. The first time you open it, your computer warns you, because the app isn't sold through an app store. Mac: click Done , open System Settings > Privacy & Security , scroll down to "Survival LLM was blocked", click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. You only do this once. Windows: click More info , then Run anyway . What's in the library Plain-text copies of openly licensed (some for non-commercial use only) and public-domain references, searchable in a fraction of a second: About 930,000 of Wikipedia's most-read articles WikiMed medical encyclopedia MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine) UK Medicines A to Z (public sector information) WikEM emergency medicine Ready.gov (FEMA) emergency guides CDC travelers' health U.S. military medicine and survival manuals Risk references for estimating micromorts: life tables and U.S. death rates wikiHow how-to guides iFixit repair guides Appropedia (appropriate technology) Q&A on home repair, cooking, gardening, the outdoors and ham radio (Stack Exchange) Each source keeps its own license, shown with every article; see the full list with licenses . Good to know It can be wrong AI models make mistakes, the small ones more often. Every answer shows the articles it used, so you can check. Private No account, no tracking. Your questions never leave your computer, and once set up it works with the internet off. Your own files Add PDFs, Word documents, ebooks and notes, like your generator's manual or your family's emergency plan, and the AI searches them too. They stay on your computer. Updates Check for updates, at the bottom of the app, installs a new version in one click and keeps your models, library and files. Battery On a MacBook Pro we measured about 100 W while it answers, for 5 to 40 seconds per question: a full battery answers roughly 100 to 300. A small generator or power station runs it easily. Update notes Already have it? Click Check for updates at the bottom of the app. 0.3.4 October 27, 2026 Reasoning setting: next to Send, choose how much the AI may think before it answers: Off, 1,000, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens, or no limit. At the limit its thinking stops and it answers from what it has, so a model stuck reasoning in circles still answers. It replaces "Think harder". When the AI looked things up but never wrote an answer, it now gets the best articles it found and tries once more, instead of showing nothing. Thanks to betsyisaac for finding this. Ask it to look something up and it searches the library, even if it first answered from memory. Answers say whether they came from memory, from articles it read, or from search results it didn't open. A warning when Reasoning or Length limit is set to no limit. 0.3.3 October 27, 2026 Mac: quitting with Cmd+Q now also stops the AI engine and frees the memory its model used. Before, it kept running in the background. Thanks to wigginthethird for the report and the fix. Library search no longer shows several copies of the same page, so the AI sees more different articles. Thanks to ahalekelly. 0.3.2 October 27, 2026 The AI no longer saves your question as a memory note. Some answers no longer open with a made-up "Sources:" line that listed the AI's search commands instead of articles. Show reasoning reads more clearly: it says when you stopped it, the time shown is how long it thought, and long reasoning scrolls with the page. Windows: cleans up an empty folder that earlier updates could leave behind. 0.3.1 October 27, 2026 Show reasoning: under each answer, open what the AI thought before it answered, with the searches and articles it read in between. It stays hidden until you click it. Most models reason first only when Think harder is ticked. 0.3.0 October 26, 2026 Memory: tell it about yourself, like a family member's allergy or the generator you own, and it keeps a short note for later chats. See and edit every note under Memory , or turn its saving off. Downloads now work on computers whose network or antivirus uses its own certificates. All releases on GitHub

title: Amazon Is Gutting Its AI Division After Sustained Failure
abstract:
Getty Images / Futurism By now, you’d be hard pressed to find anyone who isn’t broadly familiar with the AI heavyweights and their flagship models. OpenAI has ChatGPT, Anthropic has Claude, Google has Gemini. But what does Amazon have? Not a whole lot, it turns out. Unlike its competitors in the tech megacorp scene, Amazon’s standout AI model — organized under the name “Nova” — is about the farthest thing from a household name. And that’s not likely to change anytime soon, because the ecommerce giant is now gutting its in-house AI labs, Bloomberg reports . Per the outlet, Amazon is scaling back the ambitions of most of its Nova AI models and reorganizing its AI development teams as part of an effort to narrow its focus on “highest priority” goals, after its power-hungry large language models turned out to be a bust. Accordingly, the company has put most of its AI models on ice, Amazon insiders told Bloomberg . This includes its text-based Nova models, as well as video- and image-generating models, all of which have been placed in a state of “keep the lights on,” meaning they’re technically still supported, but only receive the bare minimum resources needed to sustain them. Instead, labor and computing power are being diverted toward a singular “frontier-model effort” led by Pieter Abbeel, director of the Berkeley Robot Learning Lab whose robotics company Covariant was hoovered up by Amazon in 2024. At the time Abbeel joined the tech giant, Covariant’s founders were working on AI models for robots, which lines up pretty well with Amazon’s push to automate everything it possibly can. News of the shift in Amazon’s strategic focus comes a week after it closed one of its key AI offices in San Francisco, an 80-person site specializing in research on artificial general intelligence, the supposed next-level of AI development where the tech obtains human-level intelligence and reasoning skills. With urgent questions swirling over whether LLMs can ever usher in a return on investment — let alone AGI — it may be that Amazon is jumping out of the AI hype cycle while it still can. title: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments
abstract:
Table of contents Case Study Llama Analysis of Individual writings Appendix Anna was planning to sell her condo. She had moved out in August 2024 and wanted to know whether closing in October 2026 or January 2027 would be better for taxes. An AI agent reviewed both options and correctly concluded that either date would satisfy the residence requirement for a tax break worth up to $250,000 in excluded gains. But it left out an important deadline. Under the usual rules, homeowners must have lived in a property for at least two of the five years before selling it to qualify for the exclusion. Because Anna moved out in August 2024, she would stop satisfying that requirement around the end of August 2027. If her sale was delayed beyond August 2027, she could lose eligibility. Across five attempts, Astra never identified the deadline. Opus identified it in all five attempts. The agent evaluated the proposed dates correctly, but its advice left Anna unaware of a deadline that could affect a major financial decision. A tax adviser should recognize consequential issues even when the client doesn't know to ask about them. This is the kind of professional judgment we're testing with DAYJOB: Tax , the latest addition to Surge AI's DAYJOB benchmark family . Introducing DAYJOB: Tax DAYJOB evaluates AI agents on professional tax assignments requiring specialized expertise, complex materials, and decisions that aren't fully specified in the initial instructions. Our earlier releases covered Healthcare and Finance. DAYJOB: Tax extends that work into tax preparation, compliance, and advisory services. The benchmark contains 50 environments across eight areas of tax practice. Agents receive client requests and supporting records, then produce tax returns, workpapers, technical reviews, or client advice. These assignments test professional judgment alongside tax knowledge, calculations, retrieval, and instruction following. Agents must decide what deserves investigation, resolve conflicting evidence, recognize when information is insufficient, and carry those decisions into their final work. Results: Leaderboard and Pareto Frontiers Claude Sonnet 5.5 leads with a 10.8% pass rate on the DAYJOB: Tax leaderboard , followed by Claude Fable 5.1 at 9.6% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 9.2%. We report pass@1 at a 95% rubric threshold. An attempt passes when it satisfies at least 95% of the task's criteria, which assess calculations, supporting evidence, consequential issues, and the completed deliverable. Performance versus cost We also compared model performance against average cost per trial. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 occupy the high-performance end of the measured Pareto frontier. The breadth of professional tax work DAYJOB: Tax covers eight areas, each requiring different rules, records, and expertise: Individual and family tax Small-business tax Partnerships Property and investments Estates, gifts, and trusts International tax Corporate transactions Tax review and disputes Some assignments require complete filing packages with supporting workpapers. Others ask agents to investigate transactions, review previous filings, or prepare advice about decisions clients haven't yet made. What's inside the assignments? The benchmark contains 1,789 workspace files , with a median of 30 per assignment and as many as 123. These include 1,487 PDFs, 117 Excel workbooks, 38 Word documents, and additional emails, images, CSVs, JSON records, and text files. The workspaces include filed and draft tax returns, K-1s, W-2s, IRS notices, general ledgers, payroll records, contracts, and correspondence. They also contain the less standardized evidence that tax professionals routinely work with. One assignment includes a photograph of a handwritten receipt for merchandise purchased for resale . The agent must read the item descriptions and amounts, reconcile them with spending records, and determine how the purchases affect inventory and cost of goods sold. Another assignment involves an industrial silo-services company whose client assumes it operates only in Alabama. But its field dispatch log shows crews working across five states . The job locations, crew sizes, and days on site provide evidence relevant to the company's multistate tax obligations. Other environments are similarly varied. One involves a cross-border household whose Polish employment and property records must be reconciled with cryptocurrency exchange exports, wallet histories, and historical purchase lots. Created and reviewed by tax experts DAYJOB tasks begin with real-world professional workflows. Tax experts turn these situations into realistic assignments, developing the supporting records, expected outcomes, and grading criteria. Each task undergoes a three-layer expert review for correctness, completeness, and solvability. Tax experts bring experience across corporate taxation, partnerships, individual returns, trusts, and multistate compliance. Their backgrounds include: Corporate and private-equity taxation: A tax attorney with over 10 years of experience at PwC, Deloitte, and Exxon, covering tax planning, compliance, audits, and controversy. Partnership and corporate taxation: A Baker Tilly Tax Director with experience at PwC, Moss Adams, and Windes, specializing in complex partnership allocations, consolidated corporate returns, REITs, and high-net-worth clients. Real estate and individual taxation: A tax professional with experience at Deloitte and EY, specializing in real-estate partnerships, individual taxation, and trusts. A retirement plan built on an unverified assumption A separating couple asked an AI agent how to divide their Roth IRA and 401(k). Opus 5.5 told them they weren't legally married and recommended keeping their accounts separate, with a cash payment to even out the balances. It opened one response: You aren't legally married, so neither account can be split without triggering taxes and penalties. But the couple's own records raised doubts about that conclusion. Although they now lived in Florida, where new common-law marriages generally aren't recognized, they had previously lived together in Texas and held a ceremony in Colorado. Texas recognizes informal marriages under certain conditions, and a valid marriage established elsewhere may remain valid in Florida. That distinction could change the tax consequences of dividing their retirement accounts. Across all five attempts, Opus based its recommendations around the assumption that the couple was unmarried , even when it acknowledged uncertainty. Astra recognized the need to verify their marital status in four of five attempts. One response advised: We first need to confirm your legal marital status. The client asked how to divide the accounts. The agent needed to establish whether they were married before recommending a course of action. The evidence that should have prompted that investigation was already in the files. Where DAYJOB: Tax fits Most existing tax benchmarks begin with a defined problem: a legal question to answer, a return to calculate, or missing taxpayer information to collect. These evaluations measure important capabilities, but much of a tax professional's work involves figuring out what the problem actually is. Clients provide incomplete instructions, records contain conflicting evidence, and consequential issues may never appear in the original request. DAYJOB tests whether agents can handle that end-to-end responsibility , including identifying issues the client overlooked, evaluating conflicting evidence, and deciding what needs to be done in the first place. TaxBench Can the model answer a difficult tax question? TaxBench evaluates 114 tax questions across multiple specialties, each with a defined problem and grading rubric. DAYJOB also asks whether the client asked the right question. Anna wants to compare two dates for selling her condo.

title: Harvey raised 500M for legal AI, I built the same and open sourced it
abstract:
CaseCite — Private Legal RAG CaseCite is an open-source, self-hosted legal research platform. Upload your firm's documents, ask questions, and research cases & judges — on infrastructure you control. Documents, the search index and chat history are stored on your own servers. AI features send your questions and the relevant document text to the AI providers you configure, under your own API keys (BYOK); nothing is sent to the CaseCite maintainers, and there is no telemetry. See What leaves your infrastructure . What it does Eight tools behind one login, all reading from the same document corpus. Research ( /research ) Chat over your firm's documents — semantic retrieval with keyword (BM25) rescoring of the candidates, and inline citations back to the source. Documents ( /documents ) Upload, index, and organize your corpus. Import from Google Drive, OneDrive, Box, Dropbox, Filevine, or Clio — OAuth sync, or a file picker where OAuth verification isn't needed. iManage and NetDocuments connectors exist but are experimental (untested against a live tenant) and off unless EXPERIMENTAL_CONNECTORS=true . Contracts ( /contracts ) Full contract review pipeline: analyze an indexed contract or pasted text, chat with a single contract, compare 2–4 contracts clause-by-clause against a baseline, and export a redline, a draft, or the analysis itself. Drafting ( /drafting ) Draft a document grounded in up to four documents you pick from the Knowledge Base, with server-side text extraction and PDF conversion. Set a target length for long documents (30-page agreements): you review a section plan first, then every section is drafted in its own context window against the full references and the whole is reconciled. Revisions to long drafts are scoped to the sections they touch. Case view ( /case/:id ) Open a CourtListener opinion and chat with it directly. Authority map ( /case-citations ) Map the authorities cited across documents you select. Judge intel ( /judge-intel ) Judge analytics from CourtListener. Legal tools ( /tools ) Case lookup, citation check (a scan of citing opinions for negative-treatment language — not a Shepard's/KeyCite substitute), precedents, dockets, oral arguments, and case-law trends. Screenshots Captured from the real UI against a mocked API with fictional firm, matter and
case data ( frontend/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts ). No real client or case appears. Research over the firm's documents Knowledge Base Contract analysis Citation check Practice profile. Nothing about any practice area is baked into the product.
You state what you practice, CaseCite drafts a profile of what matters in that
practice, and you edit and own it (saved via Settings). It then rides along with
every review, redline, and draft as standing context. Every AI-generated answer, analysis and draft carries a notice to verify it
against the source documents and current law before relying on it. CaseCite is
a research aid, not a substitute for a lawyer's judgment or for a citator. What leaves your infrastructure Documents, the vector index, chat history and analyses are stored only on
your deployment. Using the AI features transmits content to third parties
you choose: Uploading a document sends its text to the embeddings provider (OpenAI
by default; Voyage or Cohere if configured). Asking a question, analysing or drafting sends the question and the
relevant document text to the LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini). Case-law tools send search queries and citations to CourtListener. To keep document text entirely on your network, run both models yourself: set OPENAI_BASE_URL (chat) and EMBEDDING_BASE_URL (embeddings) to
OpenAI-compatible servers you host. Setting only the first still sends
document text to OpenAI for embedding. The full list of outbound data flows,
and how to restrict them, is in docs/subprocessors.md . License & use Copyright 2026 Thomas Unise. CaseCite is open source under the Apache License 2.0 ( LICENSE ), an OSI-approved permissive

proprietary products, as long as you keep the copyright and license notices

which the MIT license does not. Your documents, prompts and outputs are yours. The license covers the
CaseCite code, not what you put through it. Commercial support and private installs are available from the maintainer, @thomasunise . See SUPPORT.md .
Versions up to 1.3.0 were released under the Elastic License 2.0; that license
continues to apply to those versions. Quick start Prerequisites Docker + Docker Compose openssl (to generate secrets) An AI provider API key (OpenAI is the simplest start: it covers both chat and

cp .env.example .env # 1. Generate the three REQUIRED secrets (the .env.example placeholders # intentionally refuse to boot). Copy each value into .env: openssl rand -hex 32 # -> SECRET_KEY openssl rand -hex 32 # -> AUDIT_HMAC_KEY openssl rand -hex 16 # -> ENCRYPTION_SALT # 2. In .env also set OPENAI_API_KEY (or leave it empty and save a key under # Settings after signing in), then uncomment and set DOMAIN, # POSTGRES_PASSWORD and REDIS_PASSWORD in the "Bundled production stack" # section (generation hints are in the file; use DOMAIN=localhost to try it # on your machine). Set DISK_ENCRYPTION_ACKNOWLEDGED=true in .env (required to boot). # What this acknowledges: the app encrypts BYOK keys and uploaded documents # at the application layer (AES-256-GCM), but derived text (vector chunks, # chat history, analyses) is stored in cleartext in the app, Postgres and # Redis volumes — full-disk encryption of the host is YOUR responsibility. # 4. On a localhost trial Caddy redirects HTTP to HTTPS and serves a certificate

declares the persistent data volume), and read deploy/COOLIFY-SETUP.md —
you must also set TRUSTED_PROXIES to the proxy's subnet or client IPs

title: Microsoft and Epic Games Suddenly Agree That AI Is Theft
abstract:
The past four weeks have been something of a wake-up call for the video game industry. You’ve read the headlines, so you know the deal by now: AI advancements spearheaded by Claude Opus 5.5 have turned the world of coding on its axis . Decompilations that used to take months, or even years, are now being pumped out on a daily basis, and publishers can’t keep up with the deluge of vibe-coded browser ports and “native” PC recompilations. I’ve been covering and researching this over the past month, and there’s one recurring topic that keeps popping up in every comment section I read: karma . For many, this is the video game industry’s “you reap what you sow” moment, proof that the AI tools many publishers have brazenly admitted to using are a double-edged sword. It’s a tricky subject to tackle, because it comes packaged alongside so much bias. For instance, where the PlayStation emulation scene is concerned , many see it as retribution for Sony’s decision to kill physical media. Nintendo has maintained a mostly ambivalent stance on generative AI, yet some consider the explosion in vibe-coded recomps as punishment for the company’s litigious history. However, there’s a less ambiguous side to this discussion that I’m far more interested in tackling: hypocrisy. Many publishers are gleefully and very publicly advertising their use of AI to develop games, yet two specific publishers are attempting to have their cake and eat it too in this respect: Microsoft and Epic Games. Hundreds of DMCA notices have been fired off by companies in response to the recent flood of AI-powered recomps. Indie games are the prime targets, with takedown notices for open-sourced versions of Mega Crit’s Slay the Spire 2 , Maddy Makes Games’ Celeste , and Ludeon Studios’ RimWorld all featuring in GitHub’s DMCA logs over the past four weeks. These three examples are important to note because they are blameless victims of vibe-coding: games that feature no generative AI content, yet have been open-sourced against their developers’ wishes. On the other hand, Epic Games issued a DMCA notice against a vibe-coded browser port of Fortnite on October 10, and Microsoft has issued multiple DMCA notices for Minecraft , Call of Duty , and Halo -related web browser ports over the past month. I could fill this article with dozens of examples of Microsoft’s and Epic Games’ love of AI, but here are two off the dome: Epic Games’ vibe-coded shitshow of a launcher that launched on October 14, and the mere existence of Microsoft’s Copilot. Epic Games took down a recent project that allowed Fortnite (recreation) to be playable through a web browser. They also DMCA (copyright) almost every post featuring it LMFAOO pic.twitter.com/7lSK4QksBk — Backers (@BackersGamesF) October 14, 2026 Here’s a fun quote from Tim Sweeney in an interview with PC Gamer : “It’s unfortunate that so many of the AI companies operating early on had such shitty practices, you know, like one of them was found by a court to have gone off to a BitTorrent site and downloaded terabytes of data. That’s ridiculous, they shouldn’t do that.” There’s an interesting use of the past tense here; AI companies had “such shitty practices,” not have . It’s almost as if he thinks this stolen data has been scrubbed and won’t recursively be used to continue training AI models or something. But AI remains built on theft, and no major AI companies have yet been forced to engage in model disgorgement, a legal remedy that forces AI companies to delete all models built on stolen data. Also note that Sweeney neglects to mention the exact AI company he’s referring to; he simply says that “one of them” was found to have used “a BitTorrent site” to train itself. As PC Gamer notes, Epic’s artists use both Google Gemini’s Nano Banana and OpenAI’s GPT Image. Both Google Gemini and OpenAI are involved in ongoing lawsuits that allege the scraping of materials from piracy sites. However, PC Gamer’s interview with Sweeney is from June 2026. Let’s give Epic the benefit of the doubt and assume they’ve moved on to an AI model that wasn’t built on stolen data. According to an October 12 report from Bloomberg , Epic Games’ upcoming “AI first” Disney/Marvel game will be developed using Anthropic’s Claude . In September 2025, Anthropic agreed to pay $1.5 billion for training its models using illegally obtained data sourced from BitTorrent. However, while Anthropic was forced to delete the stolen data, it was not forced to delete or rework the models it had trained on said data. Meanwhile, Epic Games’ Terms of Service specifically states that you “may not[…]use code or content extracted from the Licensed Products as training input for any Generative AI Program or as prompt-based input where the Generative AI Program trains on input data.” It seems Epic Games is happy to use AI models trained on stolen data, but it’s not happy for anyone else to train AI models on their stuff. And now, on to Microsoft—and honestly, where do you even begin here? Probably with the $80 billion per year the company has committed to building AI data centers . I guess that sum explains why Activision just had to use AI to generate in-game artwork for both Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 . After all, if they didn’t save a few pennies by generating some AI slop, how would Microsoft’s shareholders know they’re getting their money’s worth? Speaking of Call of Duty , did you notice how many vibe-coded CoD web ports were wiped from the internet via DMCA notices over the past month? I count at least six. To be fair, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma stated the company “remain[s] committed” to “being responsible stewards of IP” in her Xbox Labs announcement on October 13 , so I guess we shouldn’t be surprised. Today we're standing up XBOX LABS ( https://t.co/wzXPNnCmI6 ). Here is the note that I sent to the team: Team, The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to… — ASHA (@asha_shar) October 13, 2026 But let’s be honest for a second: “being responsible stewards of IP” isn’t Microsoft’s modus operandi. “Responsible” is just a cute buzzword to throw in here, as it implies that the company gives a shit about everyone else’s IP, too. Funny, considering that time Microsoft’s Senior Product Manager suggested users use a “well-known dataset”— all seven Harry Potter books — to “generate new AI-driven Harry Potter fan fiction.” That’s just a one-off example, though. It’s not like Brent Hecht, Microsoft’s director of applied sciences, stated that the scraping the internet by LLMs represents the “largest theft of labor in human history” or anything, right? In case you didn’t know, The New York Times is currently suing both Microsoft and OpenAI, and Hecht’s comments were obtained during discovery. “Millions of people around the world will soon consider large models ‘hoovering up’ all their work to be an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions,” stated Hecht. “Almost no one intended for content they created to be used in this fashion, nor are they compensated for its use.” There’s a depressingly humorous quote in there too, sourced directly from Microsoft’s internal communications: a warning that generative AI could “significantly disrupt the employment of the very people who generated the data on which the foundation model was trained.” “Our AI content strategy has started a ‘doom loop’ that will hurt the performance of our models and the entire web at the same time,” stated another internal Microsoft memo. “It is highly unusual that an end-product threatens the economic foundations of its essential suppliers, but that is the situation we have created for our LLM business with respect to its ‘content supply chain.

title: Valve Responds to Developers Fearing AI Slop and Clones
abstract:
Valve has advised developers concerned about AI clone games to focus on community building and consistent updates. The trust built with players serves as the strongest barrier against clone games, and the features and distinct identity continually added through updates cannot be easily copied like a single mechanic. Valve's Steam Business Team shared these insights at the 'Steam Indie Connect' developer event held on October 27, stating that making the genuine version the best version has long been Valve's core principle. The event was co-hosted by Valve, the Busan Indie Connect Festival Organizing Committee, and the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA). Taking the stage were Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson from Valve's Steam Business Team, joined for the Q&A session by Matt from the localization team, which oversees translations into 30 languages for Steam and Valve games. Amid a flood of AI-generated games, Valve representatives directly explained to Korean developers how Steam handles visibility and curation. "Launch Is Not the Finish Line, It's the Starting Line" ©Source: Valve Tom Giardino opened the presentation with an update on Steam's current status. According to the presentation materials, Steam, which launched on September 12, 2003, recently reached a peak of 43.5 million concurrent users worldwide. Total Steam revenue in South Korea grew 126% over the past five years, with premium game and DLC revenue increasing by 70% and in-game purchase revenue surging by 388% over the same period. He then outlined the launch preparation process — spanning Coming Soon pages, demos, Next Fest, playtests, setting an official release date, and build reviews — remarking, "Launch feels like the finish line, but it's actually the starting line." He also urged developers not to rely solely on Steam, but to utilize consoles, other PC stores, Discord, and social media alongside it. Marc Wilkinson introduced new tools. Key among them are the Wishlist Data API, which allows developers to retrieve wishlist data by period, country, and language by specifying an App ID and date range, and the 'Personal Calendar,' which transitioned from a Steam Labs experiment into an official store feature. The Personal Calendar recommends upcoming releases wishlisted by players with similar play styles, and games must have a set official release date to appear on it. Threatening Emails Saying "We'll Copy Your Game with AI and Launch First" — Valve's Answer Demo taken down recently due to AI cloning issues ©YNOT, @Sini_Ming The question regarding AI cloning stemmed from a specific threat. One developer shared that indie developers have recently been receiving extortion emails threatening, "If you don't pay, we'll clone your game with AI and release it first." While understanding the advice to showcase games prior to release, the developer noted that such threats could make creators hesitate and asked if Steam had protective measures in place. Tom Giardino expressed regret, noting that this was the first time he had heard of such extortion cases. He started with Valve's underlying principle regarding new technologies. "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use," he said, stating that whether to use AI in development is a decision for the developers themselves. However, he pointed out that clone games existed long before AI. Spotting an interesting concept during Next Fest and quickly making a similar game or chasing trends has always happened; AI has simply accelerated that pace. He framed this as creating two challenges for developers. The first is community. Building a developer website, engaging with players, and establishing identity and trust serves as the first line of defense against clone games, whether AI was involved or not. However, he added that because it takes time and does not happen automatically, community alone is not enough. The second is continuous improvement. He emphasized that this task is equally important for small indie studios worried about AI clones and for Valve, which operates Dota. As evidence, he pointed to Valve's philosophy on anti-piracy. Valve has historically not been aggressive with DRM or anti-piracy measures. Instead, it placed weight on making the legitimate version the best version available, and he explained that Valve views AI cloning through the same lens. Giardino said, "Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective." While drawing a line on the extortion itself, he kept communication channels open. He noted that such extortion is closer to an issue for law enforcement agencies rather than a game platform to solve. Even so, he added, "If you report such cases to us, we want to look into them further and help in whatever way we can." 'AI Slop' Hits Next Fest — "First Two Days Use Random Exposure" The issue of AI slop (low-quality games made with AI) was also brought up. A developer who recently participated in Next Fest noted that complaints had surfaced on community channels and social media about an influx of low-quality games, and mentioned having experienced disappointing results personally. They asked whether Valve was aware of the issue and if solutions were planned for the next Next Fest. Marc Wilkinson explained the visibility structure of Next Fest. For the first two days of the event, games are shown to players on a virtually random basis. After that, personalized recommendations kick in, surfacing more games that a player is likely to enjoy and purchase. He pointed out that many articles complaining about a flood of low-quality games were written based solely on those first two days. He also shared the reason behind starting randomly. It is to prevent system abuse by those trying to enter early just to gain immediate visibility, and to give every game a fair share of exposure during Next Fest. "We recognize that the trade-off is some low-quality games get exposed," he said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem." Tom Giardino highlighted the shift in scale. Just three years ago, he was going around trying to convince developers to participate, saying, "There are only 50 or 100 games, so you should definitely join," but now the number of participating titles reaches into the thousands. He described it as "the pendulum swinging to the opposite side." He also pointed out that the benchmark for success varies for each game. There are titles overjoyed to gain 10,000 wishlists during Next Fest — tripling their previous total — while others are disappointed even after gaining 50,000 because it fell short of expectations. "As platform operators, we can't define what success means for an individual game," he said, explaining that Valve chose to keep the doors open for both Next Fest and seasonal sales while continuously refining page layouts and placements. He noted that this concern was not new. When Steam Greenlight launched around 14 years ago, developers asked if Greenlight games could be filtered out. When Steam Direct, the current self-publishing system, was introduced, requests came in for a checkbox to hide Steam Direct games. Every time, rather than turning developers away or trying to pre-filter good games from bad ones, Valve chose to improve the shopping experience. Giardino said, "We don't think we're perfect and there's plenty of room for improvement," but added, "Rather than limiting developer access, making Steam a smarter and more dynamic platform is the starting point of our philosophy.

title: Introducing LFM3: Every Modality for Specialized Intelligence
abstract:
Today, we’re excited to announce LFM3 , our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) built for specialized intelligence. The LFM3 model family is multimodal by nature and brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one new shared backbone. The first release of the LFM3 family covers models in the 2B parameter range. Built on a new hybrid architecture and 22T tokens of pre-training, LFM3 is far more expressive than LFM2 while maintaining its efficiency. The extra capacity in a small, fast model makes LFM3 the ideal starting point in its class for specialized intelligence: this is because it can be fine-tuned locally, it can run on any device, and it is capable enough to become a reliable expert on a specialized task. The base and post-trained models are open-weight and available today on Hugging Face , our Playground , and the Liquid AI API . Check out our docs on how to run and fine-tune them locally. Download weights Try in Liquid API Try in Playground Benchmark in Pipette New architecture for more expressivity LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention could run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. Its design came from our automated hardware-in-the-loop architecture search . For LFM3, we used this search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. We also expanded the hardware in the loop, from CPUs in one phone and one laptop for LFM2 to 14 device and backend combinations for LFM3: phones (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and OnePlus 15), a Raspberry Pi 5, laptops (Apple M4 Max and AMD Ryzen AI), and Arm and x86 cloud CPUs, plus GPUs and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. Gated short convolutions still make up over half the layers. To add capability without slowing down long contexts, we tried swapping some of them for other sequence blocks, and sliding-window attention (SWA) gave the best quality–speed tradeoff. We kept the other changes described below only where they improved quality without a meaningful speed cost. The payoff shows at long context. Per parameter, LFM3-1.7B matches LFM2-1.2B on short prompts across edge devices, and with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster. Tri-hybrid layer mix. LFM3 combines three operators: gated short convolutions, sliding-window attention (SWA), and global attention. Of its 24 layers, 13 are convolutions, 5 are SWA with a 256-token window, and 6 are global attention. The convolutions also use a kernel size of 7, up from 3 in LFM2. Head-wise gated attention. A sigmoid gate scales each head’s output, so a head can switch off when it has nothing to add. This can help suppress activation outliers that hurt quantization and improve training stability . Partial RoPE. Global attention layers rotate only the highest-frequency half of each head and leave the low-frequency half unrotated, so those dimensions match on content regardless of distance . SWA layers keep full RoPE. Sandwich norm. Each block normalizes both its input and its output, which helps keep activations well-scaled. LFM3 uses the same 128K vocabulary as LFM2.5-8B-A1B , built to tokenize non-Latin scripts more efficiently. Training. LFM3-1.7B-Base was pre-trained on 22T tokens. Compared with LFM2, the mix adds more scientific papers, repository-level code, a wider range of knowledge sources, and considerably more math. The final 3.5T tokens are a mid-training stage on curated, higher-quality data, with a larger share of agentic traces and diverse tool calls to prepare the model for agentic post-training. This stage also extends the context window to 256K tokens. A multimodal family for every need The first LFM3 release includes six models, all branched from the same LFM3-1.7B-Base backbone and all around 2B parameters. Four of them cover different input modalities (text, vision, audio, and omni), and the last two are decision models specialized from the vision and omni models. Instead of running one large general-purpose model, you can pick the one that fits your use case, customize it, and run it on-device. For a deeper dive into the performance and inference results behind these models, refer to the respective model cards. “ As AI increasingly moves from the cloud to the client, developers need models that can be deployed efficiently across the broad spectrum of AI PCs. Liquid AI's LFM3 family combines strong multimodal capabilities with a compact footprint that is well suited for on-device AI experiences. AMD has worked closely with Liquid AI across multiple generations of models, and we're excited to see LFM3 expand what's possible for specialized AI applications running locally on systems with AMD Ryzen™ AI processors. Josh Hort Senior Director & Head of ISV Enabling at AMD Across industries, we’re seeing edge AI evolve from running dedicated detection and perception models to supporting multiple concurrent AI workloads, including vision-language models, natural-language interfaces and multimodal reasoning. The challenge is delivering these capabilities within the compute, memory, and power constraints of edge devices. LFM3 brings text, vision, and audio together in a unified architecture designed for efficient deployment, with open weights that developers can fine-tune for specific applications. Developers can already run Liquid AI’s LFM2.5-VL models on Ambarella silicon through the Cooper Model Garden, and we have begun enabling LFM3 on the same platform. Malhar Palkar Senior Director for AI at Ambarella The next generation of AI will be more multimodal, personalized, and private while being distributed across devices and the cloud. Liquid AI’s LFM3 family is an exciting step in that direction, and we’re pleased to work together to bring fast, efficient, and innovative AI experiences to devices powered by Snapdragon® processors. Vinesh Sukumar VP, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. 01 / 03 Text LFM3-1.7B is a text model for local agents and specialized applications with a 256K-token context window. It is post-trained to run in agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw. It can triage your inbox, manage your calendar, research topics on the web, send you morning briefings on WhatsApp, and use tool search to find the right tool among thousands of options. Since tokens are free, dozens of agents can run continuously in the background. You can adapt it to your domains, harnesses, and tools with a short fine-tuning run on a single GPU. title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
abstract:
Apple was notified of the eMudhra incident on 17th October. As of 28th October, the developer tools Apple ships with macOS, including git, curl and python3, still trust the compromised certificates. Worse, macOS 27.2, released on 26th October, did not fix the issue and undid the workaround that users had applied by hand, leaving them vulnerable again. Meanwhile, dozens of other projects , many run by volunteers, shipped fixes days ago. Anyone can intercept any HTTPS connection these tools make. For git, that means clones and pulls from https:// remotes can deliver attacker-chosen code, pushes can be altered in transit, and your credentials, such as GitHub tokens, can be intercepted. To check whether your git is affected, run: A certificate error means your git is protected. If git lists a commit, your git is affected. Your connections to GitHub, or any other https:// git remote, can be intercepted and tampered with. To see an attack end to end, run the command below in a temporary directory. It clones a repository from a test server impersonating GitHub. The -c option redirects github.com to our test server for this one command only. The server presents a github.com certificate issued by one of the compromised eMudhra intermediates. A patched git will refuse with a certificate error. If the clone succeeds, you'll see a README.md starting with INTERCEPTED . A real attacker would not need the extra option. Anyone on the network path between you and GitHub can redirect your traffic themselves. You can replace the demo repository with any other, public or private. Keep the fake-user@ prefix. Without it, git would send your GitHub credentials to the test server. For example: curl, python3 and the other tools Apple ships are affected in the same way. To check curl, run: A certificate error means curl is protected. Apple has already protected Safari and other apps built on its networking framework. Apple needs to ship a fix for macOS developers as soon as possible, for example by removing the affected roots from /etc/ssl/cert.pem . The affected roots can be removed by hand. The macOS workaround on the main page walks through the steps. Apple's guidance states that macOS updates may revert the fix, so developers need to repeat the checks above and the workaround after every update until Apple ships a fix. Security teams should also consider whether macOS runners are used in their CI or other build infrastructure and evaluate the supply chain risk. Site published by Dennis Jackson . title: Git for the US Code
abstract:
A programmer can point at any line of code and see who wrote it, when, and what the file looked like on any past day. A lawyer reading a federal statute usually cannot, at least not without an afternoon in the notes at the foot of the section. But why shouldn't they have the same, convenient system of record? It is especially relevant given that so much first-pass legal research now runs through language models, which are often unable to utilise the proper lineage of a law, handcuffing its ability to offer interpretation. The US code Outside the titles Congress has enacted as positive law, the code is only prima facie evidence of the law, and the Statutes at Large govern where the two differ. [ 1 ] The Office of the Law Revision Counsel publishes it as a series of release points, each current through a named public law, and keeps reorganising it; a bill to enact title 41 as positive law was introduced in September 2025. [ 2 ] Which public law wrote a sentence is recorded in amendment notes, in prose. When a change took effect is often in a separate effective-date note, and where Congress said nothing the default rule is that a law takes effect on the day it is enacted. [ 3 ] The definition of a small business debtor in 11 USC § 1182(1) shows how far apart those answers can be. It was created in 2019 with the existing small business debt limit. [ 4 ] The CARES Act raised the limit to $7.5 million in March 2020 as a temporary measure, later extended to March 2022. [ 5 ] , [ 6 ] That increase lapsed on 27 March 2022, and on 21 June 2022 Congress restored it for two more years, for cases commenced on or after 27 March 2020 and still pending, which reached back over the gap. [ 7 ] The higher limit expired again in June 2024, and after the triennial adjustment in April 2025 it stands at $3,424,000. [ 8 ] , [ 9 ] For a case filed in May 2022, the release point printed at the time gives the lower limit, and only a later Act changes the answer. A history that is useful to a lawyer has to carry the text, the date each change took force, and the scope of any law that reaches back. A study from the Technical University of Munich this year found two failures in models answering questions on German statutes: they apply rules that were superseded after their training cutoff, and they prefer the newer provision even when an older one governs the facts. One model answered 24% of post-cutoff questions correctly on its own and 87% when the relevant statutory text was retrieved for it, and the authors conclude that temporal validity has to be treated as a hard constraint. [ 10 ] Other recent work trains search agents to respect the date a question is about, with large gains in consistency. [ 11 ] Asking a model to produce the old text does not solve this. When the same Munich group had a model apply German amending laws to earlier versions, the output looked 93–99% similar to the official text, but only half of single amendments and a fifth of chains of amendments matched exactly, and experts found legally significant errors in the near misses. [ 12 ] The history has to be checkable. For each pair of release points from 2017 onward, we took the public laws enacted in between, carried out their amending instructions on the older text in date order, and compared the result with the newer version. Of 365 changes across the nine titles, 361 reproduced the next release point exactly. The other four are shown with a label saying how far they could be confirmed. Each change then carries the law and the date it took effect: 261 took effect on enactment by default, 72 by an effective-date note and 29 by a date in the amendment itself. One depends on an agency determination that may never come, and we leave it out of the text rather than guess. With that record, the reader can answer the questions lawyers ask. You pick a date and get the text in force on it, with the words that read differently today marked. Each phrase is coloured by the Act that wrote it. A change to a defined term lists every other provision that uses it, and you can follow a section to see what has changed since your last visit. Limits It does not yet show a later law’s reach back on the earlier dates it covers, so for a case filed in the 2022 gap it shows the lower limit without warning that the June 2022 Act changed the answer. Effective-date notes are read by pattern, and unusual wording falls back to the date of enactment. Each change links to the law’s own words, and for anything that matters the original should be read. We're also still thinking about the right form factor this should take.
